answer: An attester must stake 16% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. Because the bridge stake is held until the atlas settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the whisper audit lists each exposure. A farm running 55 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
